subject: Meteorology
title: Ingredients for Thunderstorms
description: A 60-second lesson on Ingredients for Thunderstorms.

hook.text: Every thunderstorm needs three ingredients—moisture, instability, and a trigger to lift the air upward.

buildup.text: Moisture provides the fuel; instability lets air keep rising once it starts; a trigger sets things in motion.

discovery.text: Triggers include fronts, mountains, sea breezes, or simply the afternoon Sun heating the ground unevenly.

twist.text: All three must be present at the same time and place—remove any one, and no storm develops.

climax.text: Forecasters hunt for the overlap zone—where moisture, instability, and a trigger converge is where storms fire.

punchline.text: Three ingredients, one recipe—miss any and the sky stays quiet.

quiz.question: What are the three ingredients needed for a thunderstorm?
options: Moisture, instability, and a lifting trigger
